name: Santorini
short_description: Whitewashed cliffside villages above a volcanic caldera.
description: Santorini is a crescent-shaped Aegean island famous for dramatic caldera views, blue-domed churches, black and red volcanic beaches, romantic sunsets in Oia, and excellent Assyrtiko wines. Relaxed, scenic and ideal for couples seeking calm seaside beauty away from party crowds.
best_season: May to October

name: Kyoto
short_description: Ancient temples, tea houses and geisha districts.
description: Kyoto is the cultural heart of Japan with thousands of temples and shrines, tranquil Zen gardens, traditional wooden machiya houses, the bamboo grove of Arashiyama, refined kaiseki cuisine and serene autumn foliage. Peaceful, historic and deeply traditional.
best_season: March to May and October to November

name: Banff National Park
short_description: Turquoise lakes ringed by the Canadian Rockies.
description: Banff offers jaw-dropping mountain scenery, glacier-fed turquoise lakes like Louise and Moraine, world-class hiking and skiing, abundant wildlife, natural hot springs and dark-sky stargazing. Perfect for outdoor adventurers and nature lovers.
best_season: June to September for hiking, December to March for skiing

name: Marrakesh
short_description: Labyrinthine souks, riads and vibrant medina life.
description: Marrakesh is a sensory feast: the bustling Jemaa el-Fnaa square, maze-like souks full of spices and crafts, ornate palaces and gardens, peaceful riads with courtyard pools, and easy access to the Atlas Mountains and Sahara excursions.
best_season: March to May and September to November

name: Queenstown
short_description: The adventure-sports capital beside Lake Wakatipu.
description: Queenstown is the adrenaline capital of the world, offering bungee jumping, jet boating, skydiving, mountain biking, white-water rafting and skiing, all framed by the dramatic Remarkables range and a sparkling alpine lake. Energetic, scenic and thrill-packed.
best_season: December to February for summer, June to August for skiing

name: Rome
short_description: Ancient ruins, Renaissance art and incredible food.
description: Rome is an open-air museum where the Colosseum, Roman Forum and Pantheon sit beside Baroque fountains and Vatican masterpieces. Wander cobbled streets, enjoy world-famous pasta, gelato and espresso, and soak up millennia of layered history.
best_season: April to June and September to October

name: Bali
short_description: Rice terraces, temples and laid-back beach towns.
description: Bali blends lush emerald rice terraces, sacred Hindu temples, yoga retreats and wellness culture in Ubud with surf beaches and sunset bars in the south. Spiritual, affordable, tropical and relaxed, and popular with digital nomads.
best_season: April to October

name: Reykjavik
short_description: Gateway to volcanoes, geysers and the Northern Lights.
description: Reykjavik is the launch point for Iceland's surreal landscapes: erupting geysers, thundering waterfalls, black sand beaches, geothermal lagoons and, in winter, the dancing aurora borealis. Dramatic, otherworldly and nature-driven.
best_season: June to August for daylight, September to March for auroras

name: Cape Town
short_description: Table Mountain, beaches and winelands in one city.
description: Cape Town pairs the iconic flat-topped Table Mountain with golden beaches, penguin colonies, the Cape of Good Hope, vibrant food and music, and nearby Stellenbosch winelands. Diverse, scenic and full of outdoor adventure.
best_season: November to March

name: Machu Picchu
short_description: The lost Inca citadel high in the Andes.
description: Machu Picchu is a breathtaking 15th-century Inca citadel perched on a mountain ridge above the Sacred Valley, reached by the legendary Inca Trail or a scenic train. Mystical ruins, terraced slopes and epic Andean panoramas await.
best_season: May to September (dry season)

name: Barcelona
short_description: Gaudí architecture, tapas and Mediterranean beaches.
description: Barcelona dazzles with Gaudí's surreal Sagrada Família and Park Güell, the Gothic Quarter's medieval lanes, lively tapas bars, a buzzing beachfront and legendary nightlife. Artistic, sunny and endlessly energetic.
best_season: May to June and September

name: Serengeti National Park
short_description: Endless plains and the Great Wildebeest Migration.
description: The Serengeti is the ultimate safari destination, home to the Great Migration of millions of wildebeest and zebra, the Big Five, and vast golden savannahs dotted with acacia trees. Wild, remote and unforgettable for wildlife lovers.
best_season: June to October for migration, January to February for calving

name: Maldives
short_description: Overwater villas on impossibly clear turquoise lagoons.
description: The Maldives is a scatter of low coral atolls in the Indian Ocean, known for powder-white sand, glass-clear shallow lagoons, overwater bungalows, world-class snorkelling and diving with manta rays and whale sharks, and complete quiet. The classic luxury honeymoon escape.
best_season: November to April

name: Phuket
short_description: Limestone islands, warm seas and famous street food.
description: Phuket is Thailand's largest island, mixing long sandy beaches and warm calm water with longtail-boat trips to the limestone karsts of Phang Nga Bay, buzzing night markets, cheap and superb street food, and easy island hopping. Affordable, lively and tropical.
best_season: November to April

name: Zanzibar
short_description: Spice-island beaches and Swahili trading history.
description: Zanzibar combines long white beaches and dhow sailing on the Indian Ocean with the coral-stone alleyways of Stone Town, a UNESCO site shaped by Swahili, Arab and Indian trade. Spice farms, fresh seafood grills and relaxed reef snorkelling round it out.
best_season: June to October and December to February

name: Algarve
short_description: Golden cliffs, hidden coves and grilled sardines.
description: The Algarve is Portugal's southern coast: ochre sandstone cliffs, sea caves like Benagil, dozens of small sheltered coves, whitewashed fishing towns, superb grilled fish and some of Europe's best value seafood. Sunny, uncrowded outside August and easy to explore.
best_season: April to June and September to October

name: Tulum
short_description: Caribbean beaches beneath a clifftop Mayan ruin.
description: Tulum pairs a powder-sand Caribbean coastline with a dramatic Mayan walled city perched on the cliff above it. Inland lie freshwater cenotes for swimming and cave diving, plus the Sian Ka'an biosphere. Bohemian, warm and photogenic.
best_season: November to April

name: El Nido, Palawan
short_description: Karst cliffs rising from hidden turquoise lagoons.
description: El Nido sits at the tip of Palawan among the Bacuit archipelago, where jungle-topped limestone cliffs drop straight into calm turquoise lagoons. Island-hopping boats reach secret beaches, and the snorkelling over shallow coral is superb. Remote, quiet and cheap.
best_season: November to May

name: Interlaken
short_description: Alpine peaks and two lakes in the Bernese Oberland.
description: Interlaken sits between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz beneath the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau. Cogwheel trains climb to glaciers and viewpoints, paragliders launch over the valley, and marked trails link mountain huts and waterfalls. Immaculate, scenic and very easy to travel.
best_season: June to September, December to March for snow

name: Hunza Valley
short_description: Apricot orchards below the Karakoram's giant peaks.
description: Hunza is a high valley in the Karakoram, ringed by Rakaposhi and Ultar Sar and reached by the Karakoram Highway. Terraced apricot and cherry orchards, centuries-old forts at Baltit and Altit, glacier viewpoints and famously warm hospitality make it a spectacular, low-cost trekking base.
best_season: April to October, with autumn colour in late October

name: Torres del Paine
short_description: Granite towers, glaciers and Patagonian wind.
description: Torres del Paine in Chilean Patagonia is defined by its three granite towers, hanging glaciers, milky blue lakes and guanaco-grazed steppe. The W and O circuit treks are among the finest multi-day hikes anywhere. Raw, remote and weather-beaten.
best_season: November to March

name: Dolomites
short_description: Pale limestone spires above green alpine meadows.
description: The Dolomites are a UNESCO range of pale vertical limestone towers over wildflower meadows and larch forest. Via ferrata routes, hut-to-hut hiking, world-class skiing and a Ladin and Tyrolean food culture make them a superb, less-crowded alternative to the western Alps.
best_season: June to September, December to March for skiing

name: Chamonix
short_description: Mont Blanc, big glaciers and serious alpinism.
description: Chamonix sits directly beneath Mont Blanc, western Europe's highest peak. The Aiguille du Midi cable car delivers you to 3,842m in twenty minutes, the Mer de Glace glacier grinds down the valley, and the town is the historic home of mountaineering, off-piste skiing and trail running.
best_season: January to March for snow, June to September for hiking

name: Tokyo
short_description: Neon megacity with the world's best food scene.
description: Tokyo runs from the neon canyons of Shinjuku and Shibuya's scramble crossing to hushed shrines, immaculate parks and more Michelin stars than any other city. Trains are flawless, convenience stores are excellent, and every neighbourhood feels like a different town.
best_season: March to May and October to November

name: Istanbul
short_description: Where Europe meets Asia across the Bosphorus.
description: Istanbul spans two continents, layering Byzantine and Ottoman monuments — Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque, Topkapı Palace — over a working modern city. Ferries cross the Bosphorus at sunset, the Grand Bazaar sprawls over 4,000 shops, and the food ranges from street simit to serious meze.
best_season: April to June and September to November

name: Singapore
short_description: Hyper-modern, spotless and built around gardens.
description: Singapore is a compact city-state of futuristic architecture, Supertrees at Gardens by the Bay, colonial shophouses and outstanding hawker centres where a Michelin-recommended meal costs a few dollars. Safe, green, extremely well organised and easy for first-time travellers to Asia.
best_season: February to April

name: Lisbon
short_description: Tiled hills, yellow trams and fado in the alleys.
description: Lisbon drapes over seven hills above the Tagus, with azulejo-tiled facades, rattling Tram 28, miradouro viewpoints at every turn, custard tarts in Belém and melancholy fado sung in Alfama's bars. Sunny, affordable for western Europe and very walkable.
best_season: March to June and September to October

name: Dubai
short_description: Record-breaking skyline at the edge of the desert.
description: Dubai stacks the world's tallest building, vast air-conditioned malls, artificial islands and luxury dining against desert dunes an hour away, where 4x4 safaris and camel camps operate. Warm sea, huge hotels and a major aviation hub for stopovers.
best_season: November to March

name: Buenos Aires
short_description: Tango, steak and grand European boulevards.
description: Buenos Aires is South America's most European-feeling capital: belle époque boulevards, the painted houses of La Boca, Recoleta's ornate cemetery, milonga halls where tango is still danced nightly, and parrillas serving some of the world's best beef and Malbec.
best_season: March to May and September to November

name: Amsterdam
short_description: Canal rings, bicycles and world-class museums.
description: Amsterdam's UNESCO canal ring is lined with narrow gabled merchant houses and best seen from a bike or a boat. The Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh Museum and Anne Frank House sit within walking distance of each other, and the city stays compact, green and relaxed.
best_season: April to May for tulips, June to September

name: Petra
short_description: A rose-red Nabataean city carved into the rock.
description: Petra is a vast Nabataean capital carved directly into rose-coloured sandstone, entered through the Siq, a 1.2km slot canyon that opens onto the Treasury facade. Beyond it lie tombs, a Roman theatre and a long stair climb to the Monastery. One of the New Seven Wonders.
best_season: March to May and September to November

name: Angkor Wat
short_description: The largest religious monument on earth, in jungle.
description: Angkor was the capital of the Khmer Empire, and Angkor Wat is the biggest religious structure ever built. Sunrise over its towers, the serene stone faces of Bayon and the strangler figs swallowing Ta Prohm make a three-day temple pass go quickly. Hot, cheap and extraordinary.
best_season: November to March

name: Pyramids of Giza
short_description: The last surviving ancient wonder, beside Cairo.
description: The Giza plateau holds the Great Pyramid of Khufu, its two companions and the Sphinx, on the desert edge of a city of twenty million. Add the Grand Egyptian Museum, Islamic Cairo's mosques and a Nile felucca and it is one of the densest history trips available.
best_season: October to April

name: Athens
short_description: The Acropolis above a loud, living modern capital.
description: Athens is where the Parthenon still dominates the skyline from the Acropolis rock, with the Ancient Agora, Roman ruins and the superb Acropolis Museum below. Around them are lively tavernas in Plaka, rooftop bars and a gritty street-art scene, plus ferries to the islands.
best_season: April to June and September to October

name: Galápagos Islands
short_description: Fearless wildlife on Darwin's volcanic archipelago.
description: In the Galápagos the animals ignore you: giant tortoises, marine iguanas, blue-footed boobies, sea lions and penguins on the equator. Snorkelling with turtles and hammerheads is routine. Access is tightly controlled by the national park, which is why it still works.
best_season: December to May for warm seas, June to November for wildlife activity

name: Amazon Rainforest
short_description: The world's greatest river and the jungle around it.
description: From Manaus you reach the Meeting of the Waters and jungle lodges deep along the Río Negro, where night canoe trips find caimans, pink river dolphins surface at dawn and canopy towers open onto unbroken forest. Humid, remote and biologically unmatched.
best_season: June to November (drier season)

name: Plitvice Lakes
short_description: Sixteen terraced lakes joined by falling water.
description: Plitvice is a staircase of sixteen turquoise lakes linked by waterfalls, crossed on timber boardwalks that run just above the water. Beech and fir forest surrounds it, and an electric boat crosses the largest lake. Croatia's oldest and most photographed national park.
best_season: May to June and September to October

name: Yellowstone National Park
short_description: Geysers, bison herds and a supervolcano caldera.
description: Yellowstone sits on an active supervolcano, which is why half the world's geysers are here — Old Faithful, the Grand Prismatic Spring's colour rings, bubbling mud pots. Bison and elk graze the Lamar Valley alongside wolves and grizzlies. America's first national park.
best_season: May to September

name: Kruger National Park
short_description: Self-drive Big Five safari the size of a small country.
description: Kruger is one of Africa's largest reserves and unusually accessible: you can drive it yourself on tarred roads between rest camps, or join guided dawn drives and bush walks. Lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo and rhino are all resident, and malaria risk is low in winter.
best_season: May to September (dry season)

name: Everest Base Camp Trek
short_description: Two weeks on foot through Sherpa country to 5,364m.
description: The classic Khumbu trek starts with the airstrip at Lukla and climbs through Namche Bazaar, Tengboche monastery and glacial moraine to Base Camp beneath the Khumbu Icefall, with a dawn ascent of Kala Patthar for the Everest view. Demanding, teahouse-supported and unforgettable.
best_season: March to May and October to November

name: La Fortuna and Arenal
short_description: Volcano, canopy zip lines and jungle hot springs.
description: La Fortuna sits at the foot of the near-perfect cone of Arenal volcano. Days are spent zip-lining and canyoning through cloud forest, rafting the Río Balsa, hiking old lava flows and spotting sloths and toucans; evenings in naturally heated volcanic hot springs.
best_season: December to April

name: Moab
short_description: Red rock arches, slickrock trails and desert rivers.
description: Moab sits between Arches and Canyonlands national parks in Utah's red rock desert. It is a hub for slickrock mountain biking, 4x4 trails, rock climbing, canyoneering and Colorado River rafting, with Delicate Arch and Mesa Arch at sunrise as the signature views.
best_season: March to May and September to October

name: Wadi Rum
short_description: Mars-red sand, sandstone monoliths and Bedouin camps.
description: Wadi Rum is a protected desert of red sand and vast sandstone and granite monoliths, crossed by 4x4 and camel and climbed on scrambling routes. Nights are spent in Bedouin camps under some of the clearest skies anywhere — which is why it doubles for Mars on film.
best_season: March to May and September to November

name: Varanasi
short_description: Ritual life on the ghats of the Ganges at dawn.
description: Varanasi is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities on earth and the spiritual centre of Hinduism. Pilgrims bathe at the ghats at sunrise, the Ganga Aarti fire ceremony fills the riverfront at dusk, and cremation fires burn without pause. Intense, sacred and confronting.
best_season: October to March

name: Paro Valley
short_description: Himalayan Buddhist kingdom of dzongs and prayer flags.
description: Bhutan measures itself in Gross National Happiness and limits visitor numbers by daily fee. The Paro valley holds the Tiger's Nest monastery clinging to a cliff 900m above the floor, fortress-monasteries, masked tsechu festivals and terraced rice under Himalayan peaks.
best_season: March to May and September to November

name: Oaxaca
short_description: Mexico's food capital, mezcal and indigenous craft.
description: Oaxaca is widely considered Mexico's best place to eat — seven mole sauces, tlayudas, and mezcal distilled in surrounding villages. Zapotec weaving and alebrije carving continue in nearby towns, Monte Albán's ruins overlook the valley, and Día de Muertos here is extraordinary.
best_season: October to April

name: Hoi An
short_description: Lantern-lit trading port with tailors and river food.
description: Hoi An's old town is a preserved 15th-century trading port of yellow merchant houses, a Japanese covered bridge and silk lanterns reflected in the Thu Bồn river. It is famous for same-day tailoring, cooking classes, cao lầu noodles and a beach and rice paddies within cycling distance.
best_season: February to April

name: Jaipur
short_description: The Pink City of Rajasthani palaces and forts.
description: Jaipur's walled old city is painted terracotta pink, with the honeycomb Hawa Mahal, the City Palace, the Jantar Mantar observatory and hilltop Amber Fort above a lake. Bazaars sell block-printed textiles and gemstones, and Rajasthani thali is a serious event.
best_season: October to March
